The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of SCCH-10 Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.80,00,000/ with interest for the death of Arogyaraju S/o. Arogyanathan in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 28.07.2022.
2.

The case of the petitioners in brief is as under:
That, on 28.07.2022 at about 11.00 a.m., deceased was proceeding as pillion rider in the Two Wheeler TVS bearing Reg. No.KA02JA5815 and the same was riding by Padmanabhan from Kodihalli and when they reached in front of Gagan Dhabha Hotel, near Rani Cross, B.B. Road, Devanahalli, Bengaluru, at that point of time, the respondent No.3 / driver of Truck bearing Reg.No. KA01 AF0124 came from behind with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly took the vehicle towards right side from left side and dashed against the Two wheeler, as a result,
deceased fell down and truck wheels are passed on his right side of the body from neck to bottom and sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the SCCH-10 daughter and petitioner No.3 is the son of the deceased and they are the legal heirs of deceased.

sentences.text: The petitioners have filed the present petition seeking compensation on the account of death of Arogyaraju in a SCCH-10 road traffic accident that occurred on 28072022.
The petitioners are claiming that they are the wife, daughter and son of the deceased Arogyaraju.

13. According to the petitioners, deceased Arogyaraju was proceeding as pillion rider in the Two Wheeler TVS bearing Reg.No.KA02JA5815 and same was riding by his friend, Padmanabhan from Kodihalli and

when they reached in front of Gagan Daba Hotel, near Rani Cross, B.B. Road,
Devanahalli, Bengaluru, at that time, the respondent No.3 / driver of Truck bearing Reg.No. KA 01 AF0124 came from behind with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly took the vehicle towards right side from left side and dashed against the Two wheeler, as a result,
deceased fell down and truck wheels are passed on his right side of the body from neck to bottom and sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.

14. To substantiate the said contentions, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW1 and also examined an eyewitness and petitioner No.2 and petitioner No.3 as PW2 SCCH-10 to PW4 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.36.

The Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the endorsement, Ex.P.4 is the Death certificate, Ex.P.5 are Photos, Ex.P.15 is the Charge sheet, Ex.P.16 is the Police intimation, Ex.P.17 is the Sketch, Ex.P.18 is the Police notice,
Ex.P.19 is the Spot mahazar, Ex.P.20 is the Inquest, Ex.P.21 is the Notice u/s 133 of M.V.Act, Ex.P.22 is the Reply to the said notice and Ex.P.23 is the PM report.
15. The respondents have seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
To substantiate its defence, the respondent No.1 examined its Manager as RW1.
The respondents have not produced any documents on their behalf.
16. Ex.P.1 is the certified copy of the FIR No. 0098/2022 of Devanahalli PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that, SCCH-10 I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Truck bearing Reg. No.KA01AF0124 for the commission of offences punishable under Section 134 (A) & (B) R/w 187 of Motor Vehicles Act and Section 279, 337 and 304A of IPC.
Ex.P.19 is the seizure mahazar wherein it reveals that during investigation I.O.
has seized the offending vehicle
. Ex.P.15 is the charge sheet filed by the Devanahalli police against one Mr.Manjunath who is none other than the driver of the offending vehicle (respondent No.3).
Ex .P.20 and Ex
. P.23 are the inquest and Postmortem report respectively.
On perusal of postmortem report, it reveals that the deceased died due to the multiple injuries sustained to head due to the accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and deceased succumbed to the injuries due to the accident.
17. Though the respondent No.1 has crossexamined SCCH-10 PW1 to PW4 its manager as RW 1, nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witnesses to disprove the case of the petitioners.
18. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

In this view, Court receives support from the law declared by Susheela.G vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178948068/

Hon'ble Apex Court in para No.61 has proceeded to record the following conclusions;
(iv) In case the deceased was self employed or on fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

(v) For determination of the multiplicand, the deduction for personal and living expenses, the tribunals and the courts shall be guided by paragraphs 30 to 32 of Sarla Verma which we have reproduced hereinbefore.
(vi) The selection of multiplier shall be as indicated in the Table in Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of that judgment.
(vii) The age of the deceased should be the basis for applying the multiplier.
(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional head, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be SCCH-10 Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/ and Rs.15,000/ respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
26. As per the records, at the time of accident the deceased was aged 51 years.
Further, there is no dispute regarding the age of the deceased.
Hence, the age of the deceased is taken as 51 years at the time of accident for multiplier.

As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 an operative multiplier of 11 is applicable for the age group of 51 to 55 years.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased left behind his wife, daughter and son and they are dependents of the deceased.
In Sarla Verma case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has expressed the view regarding standardized deduction towards personal and living expenses.
where the number of dependents are 2 to 3, the deduction would be 1/3rd.
As discussed supra, in the present SCCH-10 case, claimant No.1 (wife), Claimant No.2(Daughter) and claimant No.3 (son) of the deceased are the dependents.
Hence, in the present case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.15,500/ (by relying on KSLSA notional income chart) and annual income would be Rs.1,86,000/.

If 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses, the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,24,000/.
28.
As per Pranay Sethi case, if the deceased was selfemployed, an addition of 10% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was aged in between 5160 years.
In the present case, the deceased was aged 51 years at the time of accident and was selfemployed.
Hence, an addition of 10% shall be added to Rs.1,24,000/.
If an addition of 10% is added same will be Rs.1,24,000/ + 10% = Rs.1,36,400/.
The SCCH-10 multiplier will be 11 having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of death (51 years).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,36,400/ X 11 = Rs.15,00,400/.
Thus, Rs.15,00,400/ is the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

29. As per Pranay Sethi Case, 'reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/ and Rs.15,000/
respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.'

As far as liability is concerned, respondent No.1 insurance company has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 has stated SCCH-10 that, at the time of accident the vehicle was insured under it and the policy was in force at the time of accident.
34. The respondent No.1 has specifically contended that the offending vehicle has no valid Fitness certificate on the date of accident.

The Hon'ble High Court in the judgment reported in ILR 2014 KAR 191 in between Sri Rangappa Shetty Vs. Shri Jayaramaiah and another held that; the life of an insurance policy issued in respect of a motor vehicle will be valid for one year and for every next year either it has to be renewed or new policy has to be obtained.

entities.text: Sri Rangappa Shetty Vs. Shri Jayaramaiah and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the insurer at every time of insuring a vehicle and issuing policy or renewing such policy should verify whether the vehicle has possessed all the necessary certificates including the fitness certificate and the insurance companies cannot blindly insure motor vehicles and collect premium and thereafter contend that the vehicle did not possess fitness certificate at the relevant point of time.
Therefore, the contention of respondent No.1 is not SCCH-10 acceptable.

Accordingly, the respondent No.1/insurer is liable to pay compensation of Rs.16,65,400/ with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners from the date of petition till its realization in the ratio of 50:25:25 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer the Issue No.4 Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.5:
35.

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the claimants under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,65,400/ with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
Claimant No.1 to 3 are entitled to receive SCCH-10 compensation in the ratio of 50:25:25 respectively from the respondent No.1.

The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988.

The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of SCCH-10 Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.80,00,000/ with interest for the death of Arogyaraju S/o. Arogyanathan in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 28.07.2022.

The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the SCCH-10 daughter and petitioner No.3 is the son of the deceased and they are the legal heirs of deceased.
2 deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 50 years and he was doing Painting Contractor for the buildings and he was given employment to several workers and was earning Rs.50,000/ per month.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners have put to mental shock and agony and also lost their bread earner of the family.
Further, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Truck bearing Reg.No.KA01AF0124.
The respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the Truck bearing Reg. No.KA01AF0124 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA02JA5815 was negligent in causing the accident and as such the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of said motor cycle are not made as parties.

ORDER
